name: Broken function-level authorization
mental_model: The actor reaches a function reserved for another role because the server checks routing or authentication but not function authority.
security_property: Every function invocation must authorize the exact actor role and action, independent of route naming, method, or client visibility.
root_causes: Inconsistent policy across methods or routes
signals: Privileged functions are discoverable to a basic role
Authorization differs across HTTP methods or aliases
The client hides a function that the server still accepts

hypothesis_templates.statement: A controlled {basic_role} actor may invoke {privileged_function} reserved for {privileged_role}, causing {controlled_effect} without a server-side function check.
preconditions: Both roles are controlled and explicitly permitted
The function uses only synthetic data and a reversible effect
hypothesis_templates.expected_safe_behaviour: The basic role is denied before the privileged function changes or returns protected state.
hypothesis_templates.expected_vulnerable_behaviour: The basic role completes the privileged function.
hypothesis_templates.falsifier: The basic role is consistently denied across the exact method, route, and function aliases.
stop_conditions: A privileged function affects other users
The tested role is not researcher-controlled

safe_test_pattern: Model two controlled roles, prove the privileged positive control, attempt one reversible function as the basic role, and compare a fail-closed denial.
positive_controls: The privileged controlled role can invoke the intended function
negative_controls: The basic role is denied before any protected response or effect
falsifiers: The role is permitted by documented policy
The server denies the exact function for the basic role

minimum_evidence.description: Exact role, function, method, and bounded synthetic outcome.
Role-function matrix showing why the basic role is not authorised.
Privileged-role positive control and basic-role denial control.
Clean role-state repeat for the same exact function.
Human statement limited to the demonstrated controlled function effect.

common_false_positives: The function is intentionally available to both roles
The response is a client shell and no privileged action occurs
The tested account has an inherited permission
impact_boundaries: Discovering a route is not proof of function access
One controlled function does not prove administrative compromise
minimum_impact_rules: Use only controlled roles and synthetic data
Choose a reversible or read-only function
remediation: Deny by default at the server function boundary
Test every method and route alias
programme_policy_considerations: Avoid administrative effects beyond the single synthetic action

revisions.summary: Initial role-function authorization card and two-role fixture.
